newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Defiance says Bunge raises offer price.
newsitem.headline: Defiance says Bunge raises offer price.

text.p: Miller and baker Defiance Mills Ltd said on Thursday that Bunge Foods Queensland Pty Ltd would increase its takeover offer to A$2.00 per share from A$1.95 per share and make a special dividend payment of five cents per share.
This would effectively give Defiance shareholders A$2.05 per share, the company said in a statement.
Defiance said Bunge would also extend the closing date of the ordinary share offer to May 12.
The revised offer was still below the value placed on Defiance in an independent report by Price Waterhouse, which valued Defiance shares at between A$2.65 and A$2.85.

However, Defiance directors recommended that shareholders accept the offer, given that Bunge already has 44 percent of Defiance following acceptances from its major shareholder, the O'Brien family-controlled Defiance Holdings Ltd.
"Bunge's offer is recommended because control will inevitably pass to Bunge as a consequence of the acceptance by Defiance Holdings," Defiance chairman Tom O'Brien said in a statement.
Local media have reported a split in the O'Brien family over the decision to sell its shareholding to Bunge.
Bunge Foods Queensland Pty Ltd chairman Barry Weir said the transaction would result in a business with a significantly improved competitive position.
Bunge, whose parent company is based in Sao Paolo, Brazil, would become one of three players in the Australian milling and baking market, along with Goodman Fielder and George Weston Foods Ltd.
The latest offer of an effective A$2.05 per share values Defiance at A$85.14 million based on 41.53 million shares outstanding.
Defiance shares last traded at A$1.93 on Thursday, down on the 12-month high of A$2.05.
